question: If Chevron Alignment signs are used on a curve, what shape, border, placement, orientation, and minimum mounting height are required?
model_answer: Direct Answer: When used, Chevron Alignment (W1-8) signs must be a vertical rectangle with no border, installed on the outside of the turn or curve, in line with and at approximately a right angle to approaching traffic, and mounted at a minimum height of 4 feet measured from the bottom of the sign to the elevation of the near edge of the traveled way. Their use to emphasize a change in horizontal alignment must also conform to Table 2C-4, and their spacing along the curve should follow Table 2C-5. Standards (mandatory): - "The Chevron Alignment sign shall be a vertical rectangle. No border shall be used on the Chevron Alignment sign." - "If used, Chevron Alignment signs shall be installed on the outside of a turn or curve, in line with and at approximately a right angle to approaching traffic. Chevron Alignment signs shall be installed at a minimum height of 4 feet, measured vertically from the bottom of the sign to the elevation of the near edge of the traveled way." - "The use of the Chevron Alignment (W1-8) sign (see Figures 2C-1 and 2C-2) to provide additional emphasis and guidance for a change in horizontal alignment shall be in accordance with the information shown in Table 2C-4." Guidance (recommended): - The Chevron Alignment signs should be visible for a sufficient distance to provide the road user with adequate time to react to the change in alignment. - When the Hairpin Curve sign or the 270-degree Loop sign is installed, either a One-Direction Large Arrow (W1-6) sign or Chevron Alignment (W1-8) signs should be installed on the outside of the turn or curve. Options (permitted): - Chevron Alignment signs may be used instead of or in addition to standard delineators. Visual evidence: [Image 1] shows Table 2C-5, which gives the typical spacing of Chevron Alignment signs on horizontal curves by advisory speed and curve radius (e.g., 40 feet for 15 mph or less, up to 200 feet for more than 60 mph). [Image 2] shows the full page containing Section 2C.08, including the Standard provisions on shape, border, placement, orientation, and 4-foot minimum mounting height. [Image 3] shows Figure 3G-1 (delineator placement), whose notes confirm that Chevron Alignment signs (W1-8) may be used instead of or in addition to standard delineators per Section 2C.08. [Image 4] shows Chapter 3G text likewise noting the option to use W1-8 signs in place of or in addition to standard delineators. [Image 5] is the table of contents listing Section 2C.08, Chevron Alignment Sign (W1-8). Citations: - Section 2C.08 Standard §3 (p.158) - Section 2C.08 Standard §4 (p.158) - Section 2C.08 Standard §1 (p.158) - Section 2C.08 Guidance §6 (p.158) - Section 2C.07 Guidance §9 (p.158) - Section 2C.08 Option §2 (p.158) - Table 2C-5 (p.158)
gold_answer: They must be vertical rectangles with no border, installed on the outside of the turn or curve, aligned approximately at a right angle to approaching traffic, and mounted at least 4 feet above the near edge of the traveled way.
